title: SUBMISSION OF TRUST CASES BY AGENTS

clauses.text: When submitting a Trust Case you must ensure that all particulars keyed in and all documents uploaded, including identity documents, payment slips and the instruction form, are true, complete and accurate and match the documents provided by the settlor.

You may upload the Personal Data or documents of a settlor, beneficiary, caretaker or witness only if you have verified that person’s identity in accordance with CNB’s procedures and have informed that person of, and obtained that person’s consent to, the processing of their Personal Data as described in Clause 9.

Trust documents in the Portal, including the trust deed, letter of wishes, letter of engagement, instruction form and KYC form, are prepared from the particulars you submit. You must review every generated document with the settlor before execution. CNB does not accept responsibility for errors arising from inaccurate particulars submitted by you.

You must comply with all applicable laws and CNB’s policies when using the Portal, including the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, the Trust Companies Act 1949 and any guidelines issued by the Securities Commission Malaysia relevant to the products you are authorised to represent.
You must not use the Portal to submit a Trust Case you are not authorised to represent under your agent tier, or to solicit any person in breach of your Underlying Agreement.

Statuses displayed in the Portal (including submitted, payment verified, documents generated, dispatched, stamped and completed) are workflow indicators maintained by CNB’s Internal Users. A status is not confirmation that a trust has been validly established until the trust deed has been duly executed and stamped and the Trust Case is marked COMPLETED.
Booking forms, official receipts and payment vouchers generated by the Portal are issued by CNB and form part of CNB’s records. Any copy you download is for reference only.
CNB’s records in the Portal, including its audit trail of actions, timestamps and uploaded documents, are conclusive evidence of the matters recorded, save for manifest error.
CNB may correct, reject or return any Trust Case that is incomplete, inconsistent with its supporting documents or fails compliance checks, and may request further information before proceeding.

Commission, override and payout figures shown in the Portal are generated under, and governed solely by, the Representative Agreement and its Commission Schedule. The Portal display is a record of those figures and does not of itself create any entitlement, and any dispute concerning them is to be raised and resolved in accordance with the Representative Agreement.

title: CLIENT PORTAL AND FUND MANAGEMENT INFORMATION

clauses.text: Information displayed to Clients, including Trust Asset balances, accrual views, fund management commencement and maturity dates and projected payouts, is provided for information only and is derived from the trust documents and confirmations received by CNB from Ascent Capital. It is not a statement of account, valuation or audited figure.

Nothing in the Portal constitutes investment, legal or tax advice, or an offer or invitation to subscribe for any interest in the Fund. Trust Assets are released to the Fund solely in accordance with the settlor’s written instruction and the applicable term sheet issued by Ascent Capital to CNB.

Any request to amend a letter of wishes, change beneficiaries, withdraw or re-deposit trust proceeds must be made through CNB’s prescribed forms. A message or entry in the Portal is not a valid instruction unless CNB confirms it in writing.

You must take reasonable steps to prevent unauthorised access from your own devices, must not store Personal Data on shared or unsecured devices, and must delete local copies of uploaded documents once the Trust Case is marked COMPLETED unless the law requires you to retain them.
